policies.title: Peru: Peruvian-passport citizenship treatment
policies.summary: Migration guidance confirms that a person using a Peruvian passport has no limit on stay in Peru; this is citizenship, not a foreign visitor-visa route.
conditions: The cited guidance concerns Peruvian nationals, including people with multiple nationalities, using a Peruvian passport for immigration control.
It does not determine dual-national documentation, departure requirements, identity-card use, nationality acquisition, loss, renunciation or individual border-admission circumstances.

policies.title: Peru: named ordinary passports visa-free for tourist entry
policies.summary: The current Foreign Ministry ordinary-passport table marks these nationalities as exempt (Sí) from the tourist visa requirement. This is visa-free entry, not an eVisa, visa on arrival, transit waiver or document-only route.
conditions: The policy is limited to the table's tourist column and ordinary passports; it does not classify transit, business, study, employment, residence, diplomatic, official, service, special, identity-card or other-document routes.
The table assigns nationality-specific stay limits and extension rules. No uniform duration, extension, entry count, fee, port, health, funds, onward-travel or admission condition is inferred.
Foreign visitors remain subject to migration control and the corresponding temporary immigration category; a visa exemption does not guarantee admission.

policies.title: Peru: named ordinary passports requiring a tourist visa
policies.summary: The current Foreign Ministry ordinary-passport table marks these nationalities as not exempt (No) from the tourist visa requirement. This is an advance visa requirement, not an eVisa or visa-on-arrival route.
conditions: The Ministry's legend states that No means the traveller is not exempt and requires a visa to enter Peru; the policy is limited to the ordinary-passport tourist column.

The current tourist-visa service directs affected travellers to apply through Peruvian consular offices at least 15 calendar days before travel. It does not directly establish an electronically issued eVisa, an ETA or a visa-on-arrival route for this cohort.

No duration, entries, fee, processing outcome, port, extension, health, funds, onward-travel or admission condition is inferred. Diplomatic, official, service, special, residence, transit, business, study, work and other non-tourist exceptions are outside this baseline.

conflicts.explanation: The current Foreign Ministry ordinary-passport table marks Georgia Sí in the tourist-visa exemption column, with a 90-day-per-180-days short-stay limit.

unresolved.reason: The current ordinary-passport table marks China Sí/No: visa-free tourist entry is expressly conditional on a valid ordinary passport plus a qualifying third-country visa or permanent residence. The unconditional ordinary-passport baseline is not inferred.

The current ordinary-passport table marks India Sí/No: visa-free tourist entry is expressly conditional on a valid ordinary passport plus a qualifying third-country visa or permanent residence. The unconditional ordinary-passport baseline is not inferred.

The current ordinary-passport table marks Venezuela Sí/No and states a visa-free tourist exception for nationals who have permanent residence in Colombia, Chile or Mexico. This conditional third-country-document route is not flattened into an unconditional status.
